summary.intent: Continue and complete a multi-day autonomous 'wave' orchestration process for the FSM1/cipher-box repository: burn down post-cutover engine/web/desktop issues (wave 19), then a sharing/writable-share feature build and a security-rule (rule 6 gate-verdict) audit and fix (wave 20), using Opus worktree lanes for implementation and a CodeRabbit/Greptile review chain for quality gating, with the orchestrator merging clean PRs and escalating design/security decisions to the user.
summary.outcome: Merged 67+ PRs across two waves closing dozens of issues, shipped multiple releases (v2.1.0 through v2.4.0) to staging, found and fixed several serious data-loss/lockout/security defects (content-key AAD scope mismatch, cache-vs-floor ordering, rule 6 trust-violation misclassifications, vault-root cut lockout, sharing delivery bugs), completed the writable-share and ADR 0020/0021 features, and left a small number of decisions (ADR 0021 residual, wave-timing instrumentation, open_pass stall ceiling) and a release PR pending for the user.

repo: Security rule 6 states 'a failure is a fail-closed trust violation, never mere staleness' — multiple lane agents misread this in reverse (treating availability failures as excusable trust violations); the only sanctioned exception is ADR 0021's lagging-record-unreachable case.

CodeRabbit CLI (`coderabbit review --agent`) now shares the same hourly quota pool as the web PR review (post ~2026-09-18 change) — running it burns the same budget and finds less; stop invoking it in lane briefs.

Opening a PR in ready (non-draft) state — including docs-only PRs — auto-triggers a CodeRabbit web review, consuming the shared org quota; docs PRs must be opened as draft or include `@coderabbitai ignore` in the body.

cipher-box (main repo) has `commit.gpgsign=false` deliberately set by the user to let agents commit unsigned; cipher-box-next still has signing on, causing 1Password 'failed to fill whole buffer' errors — commit there with `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit`.

Blueprint (`blueprint/*.md`) and `CONTEXT.md` changes require an accepted ADR in cipher-box-next first; ADR acceptance flow is: ADR PR merges as 'Proposed', then after the blueprint reword PR merges, a follow-up PR flips status to 'Accepted — ... in FSM1/cipher-box#NNNN (merged)'.

Durable client records (op queue, staging store, sealed stores, floor values) must decode records written by the previous release (ADR 0020); a new field needs a `#[serde(default)]` equal to the value older builds implicitly used, or a migration/new ADR is required.

GraphQL PR reply mutations do NOT expand `@file` syntax in `-f body=@file` — must read the file into a shell variable and pass `-f "body=$BODY"`, then read the posted comment back via `gh api` to confirm it rendered as text, not a literal path.

Squash-merge via `gh pr merge --squash` copies commit trailers from branch commits into the squash message by default — must merge with an explicit `--subject`/`--body-file` to avoid leaking `Co-Authored-By` attribution into main.

FUSE/desktop host error mapping: `TrustViolation` -> `EIO` (macOS/Linux) / `STATUS_DATA_ERROR` (Windows), no retry, hard I/O error to the app; `ContentUnavailable`/`Unavailable` -> `EAGAIN` / `STATUS_RETRY`, retryable — this makes the rule-6 misclassification bug user-visible as false 'file damaged' errors.

The name wave (write-plane rotation on grant cut) is NOT parallel/background as the blueprint claims — it runs inline, serially, node-by-node inside the owner command and blocks the caller; it has no durable resume marker, so an interrupted wave leaves an old name alive with no time bound (issue #1923).

`sweep_cadence` (900s) and other SyncTimingProfile constants are placeholders pending real measurement per `blueprint/testing.md`, but no instrumentation (metrics/events/timers) exists anywhere in the engine to measure wave or sweep convergence time (issue #1924).

Grant/share scopes ('grafted' scopes) are re-sealed under a new scope root; content reads and version history must resolve the seed/floor from the file's own scope, not the vault root — using the vault root seed for a file under a grafted scope causes 100% read failure for both owner and recipient (issue #1909).

code.finding: optional_u64/required_u64 used f64-as-u64 casts and treated any non-numeric JS value as 'no floor' (fail-open) — a corrupted or malicious floor value in IndexedDB could bypass the rollback bar on web only (desktop stays fail-closed); fixed to fail-closed and refuse values above 2^53-1.

resolve_child's NoUpdate arm briefly downgraded SequenceNotNewer gate rejections to ContentUnavailable citing rule 6 — this was later reverted (owner decision: option A) since rule 6 requires such rejections to always be TrustViolation.

install_unproved_scopes originally removed proved roots from the unproved set BEFORE adding newly-named roots, causing a scope root proved by one parent to be re-added to the unproved set if a stale second parent named it in the same walk — fixed by reordering (add named, then remove proved).

WriteWaveNet::interior_source and the owner sweep's open_interior_record raised the sequence floor BEFORE writing adopted bytes to the snapshot cache, so an offline read after a write share could find a stale below-floor cached record — root cause of #1913, fixed via keep_newest_last_known_good with a per-name in-memory lock covering cache-read/compare/write.

flat_root_cut / rotate_now for a vault-root read cut raised the durable read-epoch floor BEFORE the vault pointer was re-vouched at the new epoch; if the vouch failed, the device's own cold-start check refused to start ('vouched N below durable floor N+1'), a permanent single-device lockout — fixed by re-ordering to publish root, then vouch pointer, then raise floor, then sweep (#1916/#1919).

workflow: Establish a shared 'lane brief' document (`w19-common.md`) once and have every worktree agent read it, rather than repeating instructions per-lane — but keep updating it in place as new gotchas are found (CLI quota, foreground vs background skill invocation, no CLI runs, unsigned commits).

When self-reviewing before opening a PR, invoke code-review/simplify/security-review skills directly in-context rather than delegating to background sub-agents — background review sub-agents' results get orphaned/silently discarded because the parent agent's turn ends when a skill call returns, and a finished skill does not automatically continue the lane's remaining steps unless explicitly told so.

A skill invocation that spawns its own sub-agents should have those sub-agents run in the foreground, not background, or their reports go to the orchestrator instead of the lane that needs to act on them.

Before merging a PR whose branch is several commits behind a main that has had semantic (not just textual) conflicts in the same wave, do a full pairwise test-merge with the full test suite rather than trusting a clean git merge — silent semantic conflicts (e.g. two PRs each independently correct but incompatible when combined) broke `main`'s engine test target multiple times this wave despite clean auto-merges.

After any release-please merge, do not merge anything else to main until a staging deploy tag exists on that exact commit — release workflows resolve main HEAD once at dispatch time, so a later unrelated merge silently strips the release's deployability.

When an agent's report shows an interim/partial status (e.g. 'waiting for four review agents'), verify via GitHub/branch state whether the agent actually completed before assuming a stall — but also, if a background agent notification implies completion, don't act on its behalf without reading the full state, since the agent may still be running (rate-limited, retrying) and merging in that gap can orphan its in-flight commit/push.

When evidence for a policy decision is old (e.g., a comparison from ~700 PRs / months ago), explicitly flag and retire it rather than continuing to cite it as current — tooling and quotas change over time.

friction: CodeRabbit's free/CLI review quota changed mid-project (CLI now shares the same hourly pool as web reviews), which the orchestrator did not anticipate, causing wasted review slots and a false 'stale' rate-limit diagnosis before the true cause was found.

Multiple 'stall' incidents where the orchestrator's own background wait-scripts/timers died across session/account restarts, or the orchestrator simply failed to act on a fired timer notification in the same turn, costing review slots (1-2 hours idle each time).
GitHub API intermittent timeouts and DNS/network egress drops required manual retry loops around nearly every gh call.

Opening a PR as 'ready' (including docs-only PRs) silently auto-triggers a CodeRabbit review and consumes the shared quota — discovered only after it happened on PR #1915, wasting the slot intended for #1914.
GraphQL reply mutations with `-f body=@file` silently post the literal file path instead of the file contents — caught only because the user manually inspected a posted comment.

A background sub-agent's 'simplify'/security-review skill invocation spawned its own nested sub-agents that reported results to the orchestrator instead of the calling lane agent, stalling three separate lanes (G22, G23, G24) until the orchestrator manually relayed the results back.
Local FUSE-T test mounts left stray SMB server processes running on the user's own machine, producing a disruptive 'Server connections interrupted' system dialog during unrelated lane test runs.
Disk space exhaustion (down to ~219 MiB free) from accumulated worktree build artifacts (target/ dirs) mid-wave, requiring emergency cleanup.
archify diagram authoring required 8+ iterations to satisfy viewport-overflow, desktop-readability, and message-spacing validation constraints before a passing artifact was produced.
